name: What If Earth
niche: Science what-if and scale: what would really happen if something about Earth, the Moon, the Sun or your own body changed, and how long you would survive in extreme places. Promise: real physics told as a vivid story you can picture, step by step, minute by minute.
audience: Men and women 16-55 worldwide, curious, watch Kurzgesagt, What If, Fossil-style ladders. Proven by small channels: Tracer Project (3k subs) 'What If Asteroid Apophis Hit Earth' 5.4M; Ifverse (58k) 'What If Your Reaction Time Was 10x Faster' 4.6M; Universe Dimensions (98k) 'TON 618 at Different Distances' 9.3M; BeyondTheBlue 'How Long You'd Last in Every Prehistoric Ocean' 3.3M.
format: One clear what-if question. Open inside the moment (second zero, a real place, a person), then a timeline ladder: first second, first minute, first hour, first day, first year, each step with ONE physical mechanism explained so a 14-year-old could picture it, a number with a real source, and a human-scale comparison (a bus, a football field, a kitchen kettle). Middle twist that surprises. End: what this tells us about how finely balanced our real world is. No intro, no channel name, no 'today we will'.
honesty: Only real physics and published numbers (NASA, ESA, USGS, peer-reviewed papers); estimates are called estimates, with one honest hedge where scientists disagree. Never invent numbers or quotes. Hypotheticals are clearly hypothetical. Respectful wonder about the created world: no claims that the universe made itself by chance, no human-evolution claims, no astrology, no doomsday prophecy or religious end-of-the-world talk, no mockery of belief.
character: the explorer, a young man in a white space suit with orange shoulder panels, the round glass helmet tipped back so his face shows, brown boots
character_w: a young woman in a white long-sleeved space suit and a plain headscarf under the open helmet
